jacar-c04025783900.summary: The China negotiations ended peacefully; China agreed to pay an indemnity (Taiwan expedition, Beijing agreement of 31 Oct 1874). First deciphered by Ohno (2010, no. 4031); re-read here.
jacar-c04025783900.en:
"The negotiations with China have been concluded peacefully; it has been agreed that the Chinese government will pay an indemnity. We have just received the telegram."

Context: end of the 1874 Taiwan expedition. The Beijing agreement of 31 Oct 1874 (Okubo Toshimichi; the British minister Thomas Wade mediating) granted Japan an indemnity of 500,000 taels.

jacar-c04025783500.summary: Newspapers report that the China negotiations have broken down, but the government has no word; sure news will follow; give no credence to rumours. 27/29 words certain or probable. First deciphered by Ohno (2010, no. 4027); continuation also read by Satoshi Tomokiyo.
jacar-c04025783500.en: "The rumour that the negotiations with China have already broken down is reported in all the newspapers, but the government has as yet received no word of it; as soon as there is sure news it will be passed on to you without delay, so give no credence to rumours." On the same day telegram 1 announces the agreement.

jacar-c10071951300.summary: Letter from Beijing: Okubo ... the Chinese must answer by the 20th; then he will probably withdraw. 18/23 words certain or probable (22/23 with restored words that depend on two declared clerk corrections). Not in Ohno 2010.
jacar-c10071951300.en: "Consul Shinagawa says in his telegram of the 20th: I have just received a letter from Beijing: the Chinese government [...] to Plenipotentiary Okubo [...] must answer by the 20th of this month; after which he will probably withdraw." Okubo was threatening to break off and leave Beijing; the agreement was signed on 31 Oct 1874.
